images.filename: Interior Rosewell Plantation ruins Gloucester County Virginia by Frances Benjamin Johnston 1935.jpg
images.caption: View of the interior of the ruins of Rosewell Plantation by the American photographer and photojournalist Frances Benjamin Johnston. 8 x 10 black-and-white photographic negative dates from 1935, and forms part of the Johnston archives at the Library of Congress, to whom the photographer bequeathed her work in perpetuity, hence there are no restrictions on publication, as per the LOC website. Image courtesy of the Prints and Photographs Division, Library of Congress, Washington, D.C.
images.alt: View of the interior of the ruins of Rosewell Plantation by the American photographer and photojournalist Frances Benjamin Johnston. 8 x 10 black-and-white photographic negative dates from 1935, and forms part of the Johnston archives at the Library of Congress, to whom the photographer bequeathed her work in perpetuity, hence there are no restrictions on publication, as per the LOC website. Image courtesy of the Prints and Photographs Division, Library of Congress, Washington, D.C.

images.filename: View interior ruins Rosewell Plantation by Frances Benjamin Johnston 1935.jpg
images.caption: View of the interior of the ruins of Rosewell Plantation, Gloucester County, Virginia, which burned in 1916. The 8 x 10 safety film negative by the American photographer and photojournalist Frances Benjamin Johnston, and dated 1935. The image forms part of the Johnston archives at the Library of Congress, to which the photographer donated her works in perpetuity, hence there are no restrictions on publication. Image courtesy of the Prints and Photographs Division, Library of Congress, Washington, D.C.
